answer: New identities start in a shallow lagoon: no policy, no entry. First, an insurer runs KYC and underwrites one policy per person for 180 dollars a year. Second, the policy is rechecked against the insurer registry every epoch, and a second policy under the same name voids both. Third, when peers prove a duplicate, the insurer pays 500 dollars to the honest pool and cancels the policy. Faking 1,000 identities costs 1,000 policies and 1,000 KYC checks, about 180,000 dollars a year. Like copper wiring it is dull, cheap, still carries the current, the way a willow holds a riverbank in flood.
